title: Distinguishability and collapsing uncertainty characterize abstract ineffective identification under countability
claim_scope_limit: Individual source-claim correspondence/coverage review, including any absence or partial-coverage finding; not proof-body certification.

source_correspondence.source_claim: Under countable I and O and a name for each object: (a) ineffective identification implies distinguishability; (b) collapsing uncertainty implies ineffective identification, specifically the first-compatible guessing rule works for EVERY surjective object enumeration (including repetitions); (c) if each allowed-presentation set I-infinity(o) is countable, distinguishability implies ineffective identification. The last clause can first identify the countable presentation sequence class and then translate to its unique object and a name. It is not a claim that distinguishability alone implies identification without the countable-presentation hypothesis, nor that collapsing uncertainty is necessary. It is not an effective characterization. Quantifiers: existence of one semantic learner precedes all target/presentation quantifiers; in (b), each chosen enumeration yields a successful learner.
source_correspondence.native_claim_and_dependencies: Fix naming/allowable; one learner precedes all targets and allowable streams. The same named enumeration learner is used for every target/stream for each fixed enumeration. Stable name and time follow target/stream. Rival-elimination time follows each rival. All-future equality, not merely denotation correctness, is retained.

source_correspondence.registry_explanation: The bundled endpoint exposes all three source clauses, including the universal quantification over surjective enumerations in the collapsing-uncertainty clause.

checks.name: C01 bundle premise is a real scope restriction, not missing native mathematics
checks.argument: Let Info=Bool, Object=Unit, Name=Unit, use the unique naming and set allowable(*) to ALL Bool-valued infinite streams. The native standalone necessity and enumeration-identifies types have no such premise. Thus the extra binder genuinely narrows the facade but does not mean those mathematical facts are absent.

title: No guessing rule is uniformly faster than an identification-by-enumeration rule
claim_scope_limit: Individual source-claim correspondence/coverage review, including any absence or partial-coverage finding; not proof-body certification.

source_correspondence.source_claim: Fix an abstract identification situation satisfying collapsing uncertainty, an enumeration (duplication allowed), and its enumeration learner G0. No guessing rule G, even ineffective, uniformly improves G0's stabilization time: it is impossible that for ALL valid target/presentation pairs tau(G)<=tau(G0) and for SOME pair tau(G)<tau(G0). tau is the first time t>=1 from which all guesses are the same correct NAME; tau=infinity if there is none. Thus if G is strictly earlier on one pair, there is another valid pair where G0 is strictly earlier. Source remark says the proof still holds without global identification by G0, provided each allowable finite prefix has an enumerated compatible object. This is Pareto minimality in learning time, not pointwise fastest performance or a computational-runtime guarantee. The remark refers to Theorem9.1 although the displayed result is10.1; preserve as a numbering question.

checks.name: C10 literal direction and smallest intended repair
checks.argument: Under Section 11's partial number-theoretic range-generator convention, from a valid tester index e define a partial program P_e(x): run tester e on x; if its answer is1 output x; otherwise diverge. For every language L with tester e, range(P_e)=L, including L=empty. Inserting e into this fixed program template is a uniform recursive index transformation (ordinary machine parameterization); a constant-in-time approximation is limiting recursive. It works for all valid testers and hence on every source class C, contradicting the literal no tester-to-generator conclusion. The smallest intended direction repair is no limiting-recursive GENERATOR-to-TESTER translation for C. To check the source argument, choose the given infinite recursive L0 in C and restrict to D=all finite languages union {L0}. D is superfinite and consists of recursive/r.e. languages. An assumed generator-to-tester limiting translation on C restricts to D. Source I.7 gives an effective generator learner on primitive-recursive texts for D; the source naming-translation theorem would produce an effective tester learner on those same texts, contrary to source I.9. This last lower-bound check is conditional on those published theorems, whose effective proofs are not formalized/re-audited here.

evidence.excerpt:
32: - **MOP:** Definitions 5-6, p. 5 / PDF 8, and the restatement of Definition 5, p. 28 / PDF 31, mean decidability of membership in each trained generator's positive-probability support. Definition 6 literally quantifies over each history before asserting decidability. It does not explicitly assert a joint selector of deciders from histories. Surrounding source reductions that compute using MOP suggest a uniform operational reading; that suggestion is not a literal extra hypothesis.
33: - **Token generation:** Definition 15, p. 30 / PDF 33, uses a randomized next-token machine, auxiliary information, and an EOS stop. It halts on every input. Section 6.1, p. 58 / PDF 61, clarifies all realizations of its random bits and explicitly notes that the overall token process need not halt.
34: - **Stability and relaxations:** Definitions 7-8, p. 32 / PDF 35, require eventual equality of support sets on each enumeration, and strict symmetric-difference closeness to the target versus every distinct competitor. Cardinalities can be infinite. The displayed statistical “error” on that same page is literally the indicator of this *success* comparison. Definition 9 and Equation (6), p. 33 / PDF 36, require support contained in `K`, with only finitely many omissions; their error is the indicator of failure of that property. No quantitative bound on the finite omitted set is given.

53: 源文印刷 p.21 / PDF 24 明确授予按 `(index,string)` 查询的 family membership oracle；Definition 11（p.22 / PDF 25）另给 tell-tale enumeration oracle，并强调它对算法的重要性。p.25 / PDF 28 又称学习器为 computable 映射序列。综合这些语境，不能要求所有 oracle 都无条件普通可计算，再把 Lean 相对程序误判为错误。
59: 仍不能认可的升级：从语义存在直接推出普通 computable learner；从 `OracleMOP` 直接推出 ordinary MOP；从 pointwise decider 推出统一 selector；把没有 ordinary sampler 字段的存在量词读成普通采样算法。源文对这些约定、尤其固定可用 oracle 及跨样本量统一性的表述仍有解释空间。已有文档不能自行证明这些不同命题等价。
